github_release.name: Openergy 0.1.0 (alpha)
github_release.body:
First public alpha of Openergy: an open-source, lightweight replacement for Synergy. Share one keyboard, mouse, and clipboard across computers on your local network.

> [!WARNING]
> **Alpha software.** Keep another way to control each computer while you try it. Read [readiness](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/openergy/blob/v0.1.0/docs/plan/readiness.md) for what has and has not been verified.

## Downloads

| File | Platform | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Openergy-0.1.0-macos-universal.zip` | macOS 15+, Apple silicon and Intel | Menu-bar app with its daemon. Signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. |
| `openergy-0.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-unsigned.zip` | Windows x86-64 | Headless daemon and CLI. Unsigned. |
| `openergy-0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-unsigned.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64, X11 | Headless daemon and CLI. Unsigned. |

Each file has a `.sha256` checksum next to it. The Windows and Linux files also have a `.json` build manifest.

## Install on macOS

1. Unzip and move **Openergy.app** to Applications, then open it.
2. In **Permissions**, grant Accessibility (and Input Monitoring on the computer that hosts the keyboard and mouse).
3. Choose **Host** on the computer with the keyboard and mouse, or **Join** on the others. Compare certificate fingerprints before you approve a peer.

For Windows, Linux, the CLI, and moving from Synergy, see the [setup guide](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/openergy/blob/v0.1.0/docs/plan/setup.md).

## Openergy vs Synergy

Measured on the same Mac (Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.2), as a connected client of the same Windows server, with no window open:

| | Synergy 3.7 beta | Openergy 0.1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App bundle on disk | 524.4 MiB | 9.1 MiB (arm64 build) |
| Idle memory | 144.3 MiB | 64.5 MiB (app + daemon) |
| Idle CPU | 0.0% | 0.0% |

This is a field measurement, not a lab benchmark. Details: [README](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/openergy/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#openergy-vs-synergy).

## Highlights

- Works with the classic Synergy-family protocol (1.6–1.8). Tested with Synergy core 1.21.1, Deskflow 1.27, and Barrier 2.4.
- TLS on by default, with certificate pinning in both directions.
- Clipboard sharing for text, HTML, and images.
- Numbered synthetic clicks on macOS, for the macOS 27 window-focus problem seen with other Synergy-family clients.
- No accounts, telemetry, or cloud relay.
- Hosts with several displays: screen edges follow the displays that touch them, and the cursor returns to where it left after a lost connection. On a Mac host, the layout shows each display.
- Modifier remaps (for example, Ctrl on the host acts as Command on a Mac) apply to the modifier keys too.
- A key held while the cursor crosses to another screen does not repeat there, and its release is not lost.
- A client reconnects within about 5 seconds after its host comes back.
- On macOS, a permission you grant in System Settings takes effect without a restart.

## Known limits

- Windows and Linux have no graphical app or automatic updates. Wayland is not supported.
- No file transfer or drag-and-drop.
- Not yet verified: native input edge cases on test desktops (sleep and wake, mixed scaling, keyboard layouts), Windows as a client, and update installation through Sparkle.

Report bugs in [issues](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/openergy/issues). Report security problems privately through [Security → Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/openergy/security/advisories/new).
